about.title: Sources & methodology
about.intro: Clack logs the trains you ride. Timetables, actual times and maps come from open data.

sources.trafikverket: Trafikverket Open API: actual times, delays, platforms, stations and live positions.
sources.gtfsSverige2: Trafiklab GTFS Sverige 2 (CC0): historical timetables back to 2012.
sources.entur: Entur (Norway), under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD): rail timetables, stations, live positions, delays, actual times and departure boards.
sources.osm: Rail network and map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Basemap tiles by Protomaps.
sources.stationMaps: Station maps: drafted from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors) and edited by hand; the map data is offered under the ODbL like OpenStreetMap itself. Walking times are worked out from the map, not timed on site. Opening hours are as listed and may differ on holidays.
sources.onboard: On board: catering and same-day notices come from Trafikverket for each departure; everything marked "Typically" comes from the operator’s own pages, with the date it was checked.

about.delaysBody: Green: on time or early. Yellow: 1–15 min late. Amber: 16–30 min. Red: more than 30 min. A train counts as on time in your stats when it arrives at most {{max}} minutes late.
about.co2Body: Distance along the track × (comparison factor − train factor). Factors are well-to-wheel g CO₂e per passenger-km from IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute, report U11173 (2026). Norwegian trips use the same factors for now: we haven’t yet checked a Norwegian source.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Clack has no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no tracking. This is everything it keeps and why.
privacy.storedBody: The trips you add (train, date, the stations you got on and off at, and any note you write), the trains you follow, and your settings, including the optional name shown on your Passport. They’re kept under a random code your phone made when you first opened Clack, not your name, email or phone number, so they can be shown to you and kept up to date with live times.
privacy.phoneBody: That random code, a copy of your trips and the maps you’ve opened so Clack works without a connection, and small preferences like your theme and last tab.
privacy.idSync: The random code that keeps your trips is stored in your iCloud Keychain, so your trips follow you to a new iPhone; there’s still no account.
privacy.locationBody: Only when you tap "My location" on a station map. It’s used on your phone to find the nearest point on the map and is never sent to our server.
privacy.notCollectedBody: No name, email, phone number, contacts, photos or payment details. No advertising or analytics tools, and no tracking across other apps or websites.
privacy.sharingBody: No one else. To show live times our server asks Trafikverket (Sweden) and Entur (Norway) about trains by number and station; those requests say nothing about you. Ticket links open the train operator’s own website.
privacy.deletionBody: Your data stays until you delete it. "Delete my data" in Settings removes everything our server has under your code at once, and the copies on your phone.
privacy.alertsBody: Only if you turn alerts on: Apple’s address for your phone (a long code Apple gives the app so it can be sent notifications), kept with your random code and your alert settings. It is used only to send you the alerts you chose and to update the trip card on your lock screen, and it is removed when you turn alerts off or delete your data.
